programme: SOX17, LHX3, and ZFHX3 each list ESR1 (estrogen receptor alpha) among their target genes in the inferred networks, converging on estrogen-receptor transcriptional control as a shared node, with ZFHX3 independently driving pericyte/vascular calcium signalling in ischaemic stroke and SOX17 independently documented as a master/prognostic transcription factor in endometrial carcinoma.
role_in_a: In stroke, estrogen/ESR1 signalling is a known modulator of cerebrovascular tone, blood-brain-barrier integrity and neuroprotection, and sex-hormone status modifies stroke risk and outcome; ZFHX3 additionally drives pericyte contraction and calcium influx in the ischaemic vasculature (PMID 40602592), giving the module a direct, disease-specific vascular arm alongside its putative ESR1 control.
role_in_b: In endometrial carcinoma, ESR1 is the canonical proliferative driver of estrogen-dependent (Type I) disease, and SOX17 is independently reported as a master/prognostic transcription factor whose expression tracks clinical outcome and nodal spread (PMIDs 37643784, 32039004, 34818047); LHX3's other targets (LHB, INHBA, FOXL2, PITX1) place it within the same reproductive-hormonal axis.
shared_axis: Endometrium is a canonical estrogen-target tissue and cerebral vasculature is a recognised, if less prominent, site of estrogen action (post-menopausal and hormone-replacement stroke-risk literature); a set of transcription factors that converge on ESR1 in tissue-specific networks would supply a plausible shared regulatory node even without a paper studying this exact pair.
reasoning: The module is nameable directly from the data (three factors sharing ESR1 as a target) and each disease independently has an established relationship to estrogen-receptor biology, but no retrieved paper documents this convergence for either disease specifically, and only SOX17 (UCEC) and ZFHX3 (stroke, via a different mechanism - pericyte calcium, not ESR1) carry direct disease placement; LHX3 has no supporting PMID at all. The two most-recurrent factors overall, E2F8 (12/18) and HMBOX1 (12/18), sit outside this module (cell-cycle/VEGFA and NK-effector programmes respectively), so the account explains a minority, mid-recurrence slice of the concordant set rather than its strongest signal.
support: PMID 40602592 — ZFHX3 drives pericyte contraction and calcium influx in ischaemic stroke, placing it mechanistically in disease A (though via a vascular route, not shown here to be ESR1-mediated); PMID 37643784 — SOX17 pan-cancer expression tied to clinical outcome, including endometrial carcinoma; PMID 32039004 — SOX17 part of a five-gene panel predicting lymph-node metastasis in endometrial carcinoma; PMID 34818047 — SOX17 identified as a predicted master transcription factor in pan-cancer expression data including UCEC. No PMID in the material places LHX3 in either disease or documents the ESR1 convergence itself.
how_to_falsify: Perform ChIP-seq/CUT&RUN for SOX17, LHX3, and ZFHX3 at the ESR1 locus in endometrial epithelial cells (e.g., Ishikawa) and in cerebral pericytes/vascular cells; if none show occupancy or if knockdown of each fails to change ESR1 expression or estrogen-responsive reporter activity in the respective tissue, the convergence is a network-inference artifact rather than a shared regulatory node. A parallel test: compare estrogen-dependent neuroprotection (e.g., MCAO outcome with and without estrogen) in ZFHX3-knockdown versus wild-type cells/animals — no ESR1-pathway difference would undercut the stroke-side link.
caveats: Tissue pairing is anatomically distant (blood-derived networks for stroke vs. endometrial tumour tissue for UCEC), and the 18 patient-group comparisons rest on only 2 independent cohort pairs, which limits how far concordance can be generalised. HLX was removed as tissue-generic despite high recurrence (0.67) — its absence from the account is due to that filter, not an oversight. STAT2 was also removed as tissue-generic, ruling out an interferon-pathway story. None of the single-view factors (NANOG, HOXB13, etc.) recurred enough to support a reprogramming/stemness narrative, and none are used here. The account covers only 3 of 12 concordant factors; E2F8, HMBOX1, SOX10, GLIS3, ETV4, TP73, KLF15, RFXANK, and ONECUT2 belong to other, unconnected programmes (cell-cycle/VEGFA, NK-immune effector, glial/neural-crest, apoptosis/p53, MHC-II antigen presentation, metabolism, ETS/invasion) that this account does not explain.
